purpose.is: The card builder turns a record whose status code says "the owner acts" into exactly one decision card on the owner's page, built by template from the record, checked against the owner's prose standard, and posted only when the tier's watcher lamp is alive.
purpose.is-not: It never composes prose with an LLM, never asks a question the code table does not name, and never posts twice for one cause.
purpose.why: Today a decision exists only if an agent remembered to run make ask (L08 finding 3); cards replaced each other wholesale; and a card could go up unwatched (C32). The owner ruled the system lane on C40: cards come from records by status code.
purpose.decisions: D12 (C40), D11 code does mechanical jobs (C39), D15 the owner holds the line through cards (C50), D20 bearings is the one surface (C51), V17 standing policies with deadline and default, no-bureaucracy-creep (bundle what is mechanical, ask only what changes the build, recommend so a yes is one word).

The builder is level-triggered: on every scheduler tick (N-06, 1 s) it lists owner-acts records with no card and no held-card expiry in the future, so a tick lost or a lamp that comes back late never strands a decision.

mechanism.where: Go service (D01), package internal/owner/cards, inside coq.service; one goroutine driven by the scheduler tick (N-07 shape: list, compare, act). Templates in the repository at tools/bearings/config/cards.template.json, validated by tools/bearings/config/cards.template.schema.json at make lint, loaded with Reload (N-43 shape) so a text change is a pull request and a reload, never a restart.
mechanism.step: On each tick, select causes by query, not by a watermark: records with acts=owner in the loaded code table (N-43 code.table) that have no card and no card.merged naming them as cause. A cause whose last outcome is card.held is selected again once its retry_at has passed; a cause with card.unwatched is selected again on every tick (the post goes up on the first tick a lamp is alive); a cause with card.refused is selected again when the template table's version is newer than the one the refusal names. Terminal is only card and card.merged; refused and unwatched are retryable states, so a fixed template or a returning lamp posts the card with no hand step. Bounded: the query uses the index on (kind, code) of the open causes, and the per-tick cap applies.

Dedupe: one card per (ticket, kind, code) open at a time (owner.mjs rule carried forward). A second dead record for the same ticket while its card is open adds a line to the open card's about count, not a new card; the second cause is recorded as card.merged 100 naming the open card, committed with operation key N-28/card.merged/merged:<cause id>/r1, so a re-run of the tick replays it and the cause is never re-selected.

Build the card from the template row keyed (kind, code): about, decide, options and rec with placeholders filled from the record (ticket id plus full title from the ticket record in the store, attempt, reason, sha short, the tier). A template row with a policy ref sets deadline and default from the standing policies table (V17; shared/seat-contract.xml#standing-policies) only when every option's effect is none or ticket.unblock; a row whose options carry any other effect is owner-only (owner_only true) and gets no deadline and no default, and make lint refuses a policy ref on such a row (shared/authority.xml#relayable-rulings).

Run the card checker (internal/owner/cardcheck, the same rules as tools/bearings/scripts/sitrep-check.mjs for prose, plus the card rules below). A violation writes card.refused 400 and an alert (a system defect: the template is wrong) and the record is not carded until the template is fixed and reloaded; the cause stays listed so it cards after the fix.

Gate: read watcher.alive for the target page; state alive and beat age under 15 s. Otherwise write card.held 423 with attempt n and retry_at = now plus 10 s times 2 to the power (n minus 1), capped at 5 min (the N-11 backoff), and stop for this cause. At attempt 3 held, write card.unwatched 500 instead, which is an alert to N-41 and, once live, a phone push (N-52), and the cause stays listed so the card posts on the first tick after a lamp returns.

Post: one Store.Commit of the card record with operation key N-28/card.post/<cause id>/r1 and the card number from the counter card_number taken in the same transaction (N-01). A replay returns the card already posted (see many agents); stop.

Delivered: the first card.shown 200 for the card on its tier (N-31, the page's ack carries the card ids it drew) stamps delivered_at on the card entity, which the deck and the Controls open-cards panel show; nothing waits on it. Close: when a ruling record (N-29) or a policy.applied 200 names the card, write card.done 200 with the ruling id. The page removes it from the deck on the push; the phone bridge sends nothing more.
mechanism.text: Why the builder never asks what the table does not name: no-bureaucracy-creep. Everything that can be a rule is a rule; the architect decides what a careful colleague would; the owner's cards are the few that change the build or stop the line. Adding a card kind is a row in shared/status-codes.xml with acts=owner and a template row, reviewed as a pull request.

Why posted to a tier and not to "the page": uat tiers carry the promotion confirm card (N-48) for a page change; stable carries everything else; a dev tier carries test cards only. The tier field keeps a confirm card for a dev page off the owner's stable deck.

card-shape.rule: about: one line, "<topic> - <the one fact>", 200 chars max (owner 2026-10-12 16:22Z: right to the point, spacious).
decide: one question, 300 chars max, every sentence 15 words or fewer, no semicolon (STD-owner-comms-001).

options: 2 to 4; label 1 to 4 words (80 chars max); then 8 words or fewer (300 chars max) saying what happens; the recommended one is marked and comes first unless the template says otherwise, so a yes is one word.
A ticket is never named without its full title; the title goes on its own line under about and never counts against a word budget.
No record id, pid, pane id or path in the text; those stay in the cause record the page links to behind a fold.
No em dash; UTC; ids never reused once shown.
Bad news first, plainly, in the same voice as good news.
An owner-only card (owner_only true) carries no deadline, no default and no option labelled with an owner word as a suggestion; the card asks, the owner answers.
card-shape.checker: internal/owner/cardcheck returns one VIOLATION line per broken rule and the builder refuses on any; make lint runs the checker over every template row with sample data so a bad template never reaches a tick.

standing-cards.s: What broke (review NF-D2, 2026-10-15): neither halt path produced a ruling; the inbox forwarded USERHALT as source controls, which N-29 accepted only from the page service, and the Controls screen posted its own card per action under a card id N-29 could not parse.

The rule: at bring-up (bootstrap B1, shared/cut-over.xml#bootstrap) this node posts one standing card per lever, once, with operation key N-28/card.standing/<lever>/r1: halt (USERHALT, effect control.halt), resume (USERGO, control.resume), gofactory (GOFACTORY, gofactory) and build-mode (build-mode.set on or off). Each is owner_only, has no deadline and no default, and never gets card.done; its id is the entity standing:<lever> that N-30 and N-42 read.

A standing card is answered once per action (N-29: one ruling per card and action id): the Controls lever (N-42) answers with its client action id, the inbox (N-30) with the owner.message id; nothing else may answer it. The deck draws standing cards as the lever row, not as open decisions.

standing-cards.s: Rejected: a card per action posted by the screen itself (two card writers, and an id N-29 could not parse); answering a pseudo card whose id is the action id (no card record behind it, so nothing proves the lever was offered).

start.text: The builder is a goroutine of coq.service (N-06 unit.start); it has no unit of its own and nothing to type. It is live when coq.service is live and its code table is loaded; it stays dark (build mode, N-44) until its own go-live ticket flips cards.enabled in the service config with the named proof: one real dead record carded on stable while the old make ask path still exists, then make ask retired.

wait.fallback: skip this tick, count builder_tick_skipped, next tick retries; 3 skips in a row is an unhealthy record from N-06
keep the last good table; write code.table.reload.failed 500 (N-43 kind); the tick continues with the old table
treat as not alive: card.held 423 (never post unwatched on a doubt)
retry 3 times (1, 2, 4 s); then card.post.failed 500 alert; the cause stays listed for the next tick

wait.what: a lamp returning while a card is held
wait.timeout: none needed: the backoff is bounded at 5 min and the third hold is an alert
wait.fallback: card.unwatched 500 reaches the owner through the alerts screen and the phone bridge, and systemd is restarting the watcher meanwhile (N-27)

wait.timeout: a deadline only when a standing policy row names one on a relayable card; an owner-only card has none and escalates once by alert.aged; nothing else in the line waits with it
wait.fallback: relayable card: policy.applied 200 with the default option, which N-29 records as a ruling with source policy (effects none or ticket.unblock only); the owner may overturn through a fresh card when the ruling is reopenable. Owner-only card: no default ever; one alert.aged escalation, then it waits

waits.no-cog: The cog that could stall this node is a missing watcher. Timeout: three held attempts. Fallback: the alert path that needs no lamp (N-41 draws alerts from records, N-52 pushes to the phone) and systemd bringing the watcher back. A second cog is the owner himself: a card with no policy row waits, but the line does not; merge.hold, build-mode and the exit test carry on by their own rules.

retries.rule: Every store call retries 3 times with backoff then writes a 500 record and continues; the level-triggered tick is the recovery for everything the builder dropped, because a cause with no card is found again next tick.
A dead record becomes exactly one card, never a repeat (dag.md rule 3): the operation key N-28/card.post/<cause id>/r1 and the (ticket, kind, code) dedupe make a retry after a crash a no-op.

many-agents-at-once.readers: Any number of seats read this volume; the template file is edited by one ticket at a time (one file, one in-flight ticket) and reviewed as a pull request with make lint running the checker.
many-agents-at-once.workers: Build tickets from this node touch internal/owner/cards, internal/owner/cardcheck, tools/bearings/config/cards.template.json and its schema; the page (N-32), the intake (N-29) and the lamp (N-27) own different files.

collision.what: two builder instances (a second coq.service during an upgrade)

many-agents-at-once.collision: The commit under N-28/card.post/<cause id>/r1 lands once; the loser's commit replays (200) and returns the winner's card. The card number comes from a transactional counter in N-01, so two posts can never share or skip a number.

collision.what: a cause record and its ruling land in the same tick

many-agents-at-once.collision: The ruling names a card id; if the card is not yet posted the ruling is refused by N-29 as answer.rejected 400 (unknown card), which cannot happen for a page answer (the page only shows posted cards) and is correct for a relayed answer that raced the post.

collision.what: twenty records with acts=owner in one tick (a crash storm)

many-agents-at-once.collision: The dedupe per (ticket, kind, code) and a per-tick cap (config cards.max_per_tick, default 5) keep the deck readable; the rest card on later ticks in cause order; the cap and the backlog depth are counters on the health line so a storm is visible, not hidden.

collision.what: the owner answers a card on two devices at once

many-agents-at-once.collision: That is N-29's compare-and-swap: one ruling, the second gets an ack saying already answered.
many-agents-at-once.test: tests run two builder goroutines over one store with the same cause list under the fake clock: exactly one card per cause, numbers dense and increasing, a held card posts on the first tick after a lamp returns, the third hold writes card.unwatched.

look.rule: A card draws as a Factorio GUI frame on the bearings page: dark steel panel (#313031 centre, #4D4643 edge, #231C19 inner ring) with the caption in cream-orange #FFE6C0 at heading-1 weight, options as buttons with the orange hover #E69C2B and the recommended one carrying the slot glow #FFAE00 at 50 percent; progress to a deadline, when one exists, as a production bar in #2BE327; a card whose cause is a 500 or 422 carries the heat bar red #DA4535 on its header line. Font Titillium Web (OFL). Values only from the art inventory section 4.3 and 4.4; original 9-slice art, no Wube or BiusArt pixel. The same card on the phone (430 CSS px, safe areas, build-notes 2 and 3) is the same card, only stacked.
look.check: The page tests render one card of each cause class on the dev tier and the screenshots go to the owner before the uat confirm card; the Playwright probe asserts the colour values of the frame, caption and recommended option, so a theme regression fails the suite, not the owner's eye.
